## Description {#details}

A class template for a list of nodes which store the links inside themselves as intrusive nodes.

<ParametersList title="Template Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="T">Type of object that includes the intrusive node.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="N">Type of intrusive node with the next &amp; previous links.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="MP">Name of the intrusive node member in object T.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="L">Type of the links node (one of <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/double-list-links">double&#95;list&#95;links</Link></code> or <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/static-double-list-links">static&#95;double&#95;list&#95;links</Link></code>).</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="U">Type stored in the list, derived from T.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>
This class implements an intrusive doubly linked list, where each object stores its own link node as a member. The list maintains a pair of head and tail pointers, allowing efficient insertion, removal, and iteration. The intrusive approach eliminates the need for separate node allocations, as the links are embedded within the objects themselves.

The template parameter <code>MP</code> specifies the member pointer to the intrusive node within the object, enabling the list to compute the address of the parent object from the node pointer. This design supports both regular and statically allocated lists, depending on the type used for <code>L</code>.

Iterators provide access to the objects in the list, supporting bidirectional traversal.


<SectionUser title="Example">

</SectionUser>


<ProgramListing extension="cpp">

<CodeLine><Highlight kind="keyword">namespace </Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">os = micro&#95;os&#95;plus;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight><Highlight kind="keyword">using </Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">threads&#95;list = os::utils::intrusive&#95;list&lt;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  thread, os::utils::double&#95;list&#95;links, &amp;thread::child&#95;links&#95;&gt;;</Highlight></CodeLine>

</ProgramListing>

For statically allocated lists, set L=<Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/static-double-list-links">static&#95;double&#95;list&#95;links</Link>.

## Public Constructors

### intrusive&#95;list() {#a05efb4b473471f15d792fb4042435bc2}

<MemberDefinition
  template={<>template &lt;class T, class N, N T::&#42; MP, class L = double&#95;list&#95;links, class U = T&gt;</>}
  prototype={<>micro&#95;os&#95;plus::utils::intrusive&#95;list&lt; T, N, MP, L, U &gt;::intrusive&#95;list ()</>}
  labels = {["constexpr"]}>
Construct an intrusive doubly linked list.

The default constructor for <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/intrusive-list">intrusive&#95;list</Link></code> creates an empty intrusive list. No initialisation of internal pointers is performed here; for statically allocated lists, the pointers are expected to be zero-initialised by the runtime, while for dynamically allocated lists, initialisation is handled by the base class or explicit methods.


<SectionUser title="The rule of five">
The copy constructor, move constructor, copy assignment operator, and move assignment operator are explicitly deleted to prevent accidental copying or moving of <Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/intrusive-list">intrusive&#95;list</Link> objects. This ensures the integrity of the list structure, as duplicating or moving lists could result in invalid or inconsistent links within the list.
</SectionUser>

Computes and returns a pointer to the parent object that contains the intrusive node referenced by the given node pointer. ### links&#95; {#a22d5f70c0589acc1c18d10e740c7a599}

<MemberDefinition

  prototype={<>links&#95;type micro&#95;os&#95;plus::utils::double&#95;list&lt; N, double&#95;list&#95;links &gt;::links&#95;</>}
  labels = {["protected"]}>
The list top node used to point to <b>head</b> and <b>tail</b> nodes.

This member stores the internal links node for the list. The <b>next</b> pointer of this node points to the head of the list, and the <b>previous</b> pointer points to the tail. For an empty list, both pointers refer to the node itself, simplifying list management and boundary checks.
